text: Module eight. What happens between doing the work and being paid for it.
It starts with the rates. What each activity pays — watering, mulching — and the date each version came into force.
Rates are published as a version, never edited in place. Changing what watering pays does not rewrite history: work keeps the rate that was in force when it was done.
Then a run is compiled. It reads the rates in force, sums the work in the period, and subtracts anything held. Nothing is paid yet — it is arithmetic, not money.
And a run has to be approved by somebody other than whoever compiled it. That is the whole reason this is three steps rather than one button.
Money can also be held back, from one caretaker or a whole zone, with a reason recorded against it.
A hold withholds everything for that subject from every run, and only a person can lift it. It does not expire when the problem is fixed.
On the phone, all of that arrives as one screen. Paid monthly, via M-Pesa.
And here it is empty — while the same caretaker's profile shows forty-five logs this month.
Which is the thing worth telling somebody plainly. Logged work is not paid work. The money appears when a run covering it has been compiled, approved and disbursed.
Five pages. Three steps, two people, and one screen that has to explain a wait.
